questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: A year on Mercury lasts just 88 Earth days.

questions.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon in July 1969, with Buzz Aldrin close behind him.

questions.question: Which planet has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot, bigger than the whole Earth?
questions.explanation: The Great Red Spot has been swirling for at least 150 years.

questions.question: What do we call a rock from space that lands on Earth?
questions.explanation: It is a meteor while it streaks across the sky, and a meteorite once it lands.

questions.question: Roughly how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.explanation: Sunlight travels about 150 million kilometres to reach us, in a little over 8 minutes.

questions.question: Which planet is this?
questions.explanation: Saturn is so light for its size that it would float, if you could find a bath big enough.

media.alt: A pale golden planet seen from space

questions.question: Which planet is this?
questions.explanation: Neptune has the fastest winds in the Solar System, blowing at more than 2,000 km/h.

media.alt: A pale blue planet against black space

questions.question: What is the name of the galaxy we live in?
questions.explanation: On a really dark night you can see the Milky Way as a faint, glowing band across the sky.

questions.question: Which British astronaut ran the London Marathon on a treadmill in space in 2016?
questions.explanation: Tim Peake ran it strapped to a treadmill aboard the International Space Station, while the real race went on below.

questions.question: What is at the centre of our Solar System?
questions.explanation: The Sun holds more than 99% of all the stuff in the Solar System.

questions.question: Roughly how long does the Moon take to travel once round the Earth?
questions.explanation: It takes about 27 days, and the word 'month' comes from the same old word as 'Moon'.

questions.question: Why does the Moon seem to change shape during the month?
options: We see different amounts of its sunlit side
Earth's shadow covers part of it
questions.answer: We see different amounts of its sunlit side
questions.explanation: Half the Moon is always lit by the Sun; as it travels round us, we see more or less of that bright half.

questions.question: Which planet did NASA's Perseverance rover land on in 2021?
questions.explanation: Perseverance even carried a small helicopter called Ingenuity, the first aircraft to make a powered flight on another planet.

questions.question: Astronauts on the International Space Station see which of these about 16 times every day?
questions.explanation: The space station zooms round the Earth about every 90 minutes, so the Sun rises and sets again and again.

questions.question: How many planets are there in our Solar System?
questions.explanation: Pluto was counted as the ninth planet until 2006, when it was renamed a dwarf planet.

questions.question: Who was the first person to travel into space?
questions.explanation: Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth once in Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961.

questions.question: Which planet spins on its side, its axis tilted by about 98 degrees?
questions.explanation: Uranus rolls round the Sun on its side, probably knocked over by a giant collision long ago.

questions.question: Which is the largest moon in the Solar System?
questions.explanation: Jupiter's moon Ganymede is even wider than the planet Mercury.

questions.question: Who became the first British person in space, in 1991?
questions.explanation: Helen Sharman spent about eight days in space in May 1991, most of them aboard the Soviet space station Mir.

questions.question: Which is the hottest planet in the Solar System?
questions.explanation: Venus is hotter than Mercury, even though it is further from the Sun, because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps the heat.

questions.question: Which moon is this?
questions.explanation: Io is the most volcanic world in the Solar System, squeezed and heated by Jupiter's gravity.

media.alt: A yellow and orange speckled moon

questions.question: Which dwarf planet is this, photographed close up by New Horizons in 2015?
questions.explanation: The pale, heart-shaped plain on Pluto is named Tombaugh Regio, after Clyde Tombaugh, who discovered Pluto in 1930.

media.alt: A small icy world with a pale patch

questions.question: Which moon is this?
questions.explanation: Titan is the only moon with a thick atmosphere, and it has lakes of liquid methane and ethane.

media.credit: Photo: NASA/JPL-Caltech/SSI/Kevin M. Gill, CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which planet takes longer to spin once on its axis than to travel once round the Sun?
questions.explanation: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to spin once, but only about 225 to orbit the Sun, and it spins backwards too.

questions.question: Which is the nearest star to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Proxima Centauri is about 4.2 light years away, so the light we see from it left more than four years ago.

questions.question: Which planet's largest moon, Triton, orbits in the opposite direction to the planet's spin?
questions.explanation: Triton is the only large moon that orbits backwards, a clue that Neptune probably captured it.

questions.question: Who was the first woman in space, in 1963?
questions.explanation: Valentina Tereshkova orbited the Earth 48 times in Vostok 6.

questions.question: Which gas makes up most of the Sun?
questions.explanation: In the Sun's core, hydrogen is fused into helium, and that is what makes it shine.

questions.question: What was the name of the NASA programme that landed people on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Twelve astronauts walked on the Moon during the Apollo missions between 1969 and 1972.

questions.question: Which astronomer discovered Uranus in 1781?
questions.explanation: Herschel spotted it from his garden in Bath and wanted to name it after King George III.
